title: Telemetry Orchestrator: trace hooks, metric shaping, and adaptive pager policy
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our current SLO/alert stack raises a large number of noisy pages during short correlated latency bursts and rollout events. Traces are under-sampled for mid-severity errors and there is no coordinated shaping of metrics and logs before they hit the alert rules. Goal: Build a small orchestration layer (Telemetry Orchestrator) that ties trace hooks, a metric shaping pipeline, and an 'adaptive pager' policy together so alerts are more signal-rich and pages are fewer and more actionable. This work spans three deliverables: 1) trace hook enhancements to enable severity-driven sampling and provenance tags; 2) a lightweight metric/log shaping stage (aggregation, seasonality normalization, and dedup key generation) upstream of alerting rules; 3) adaptive pager policy that uses short-window risk scoring (risk-burst windows) plus anomaly signals to suppress or escalate pages with runbook context.
acceptance_criteria: Trace hook can attach provenance and risk_score tags to sampled traces (>=95% of service routes instrumented)
Metric shaping pipeline normalizes 95th/99th latency histograms and emits deduplication keys used by alert dedupe logic
New adaptive pager policy reduces low-actionable page rate by >=35% in the canary environment without increasing time-to-detect for Sev2+/SLO-violations
Anomaly detector provides a confidence score and explanation field that is surfaced in the pager notification
Feature flags exist to toggle orchestration per-service and per-environment; rollback path documented
implementation_notes: Tracing: add two new small fields to span metadata: telemetry.provenance (string) and telemetry.risk_score (float); risk_score computed by a local shim that consumes HTTP status, duration, and user-facing-route mapping
Sampling: implement severity-driven sampling in the trace agent so we sample a higher fraction for requests with risk_score >= 0.6 and for requests that hit internal error tags
Metric shaping: implement a stream transformer in the telemetry ingestion pipeline to perform per-route normalization using a 1h seasonal baseline and emit 'normalized_latency_p50/p95/p99' metrics
Deduplication keys: combine service/route/error_class/short_stack_fingerprint to generate dedupe_key used by the pager engine

Anomaly detection: initial model is a streaming Holt-Winters baseline with a lightweight anomaly classifier (logistic) that incorporates metadata from traces; model runs in the metrics pipeline to provide anomaly_score and explanation
Pager policy: implement short 'risk-burst' windows (30s/2m/10m) that compute a risk-aggregate; map to page, slack, or silent notification based on thresholds and anomaly_score
Rollout: gate by feature flag per-service, start with staging -> canary (20% traffic for 48h) -> gradual ramp; collect false positive rate and time-to-detect metrics
Observability: new dashboards for risk-burst exposures, page latency vs action, and trace coverage should be added to Console; create alerts for data-loss or shaping pipeline lag > 5m

2025-02-17: Metric shaping transformer POC completed; emits normalized p50/p95/p99 and dedupe_key; hooking into the canary alert rule for validation
2025-02-20: Pager policy draft implemented behind feature flag; canary run configured for 'public-api' service on staging cluster
2025-02-22: Canary day 2: observed 42% reduction in low-actionable pages for the canary service; some missed transient spikes noted — tuning anomaly classifier next
